title: Dose 10 mL from a bottle-top dispenser, stop to stop
instruction: Dispense one 10 mL dose of the solution from the bottle-top dispenser into the empty 50 mL tube, then stand the tube back in the rack and let go.
context: Why: dosing a set volume of buffer, acid or solvent straight from the reagent bottle with a bottle-top dispenser is one of the commonest manual steps in QC, teaching and research labs, and lab automation still leaves it to people: a robot that can work the dispensers labs already own, holding the vessel to the spout with one hand and stroking the piston with the other, can prepare buffers and media unattended. The maker's manual for this fixed-volume 10 mL dispenser says: hold the discharge-tube orifice on the inner wall of the receiving vessel, lift the piston gently to the upper stop, press it slowly and steadily to the lower stop, and always leave it parked at the lower stop; the stated accuracy holds only when both stops are reached. A short lift doses short; a stream fired from the spout into a vessel below splashes. Done by: laboratory technicians and research assistants preparing reagents and media.
setup: A 600 x 400 mm PP catch tray (15 mm lips) lies on the table, centred 250 mm in front of the robot and 50 mm right of the centre line. On it, a 200 x 200 mm, 3 mm rubber mat with a marked cross 200 mm in front of the robot on the centre line. On the cross: a 500 mL borosilicate GL45 media bottle (86 mm OD, 176 mm tall) holding 400 mL water, and screwed on its neck a fixed-volume 10 mL bottle-top dispenser (BRAND Dispensette S, Cat. 4600 240; PP housing, borosilicate cylinder, PTFE discharge tube; primed; screw cap off the discharge tube). Bottle, water and dispenser weigh 1.2 kg. The 7 mm discharge tube leaves the 50 mm valve block 228 mm above the mat pointing to the robot's right, runs horizontally to a bend 85 mm from the bottle axis, then turns straight down for 20 mm to the orifice (208 mm above the mat). The piston is the dispenser's upper housing, a 40 mm wide sleeve 60 mm tall on the bottle axis: parked at its lower stop its top is 300 mm above the mat; it lifts 40 mm to the fixed 10 mL upper stop with 4 N of friction each way and stays where it is left. On the tray to the right: a PP rack for 50 mL tubes (170 x 45 x 60 mm, 120 g), long side front to back, centred 200 mm in front of the robot and 150 mm right of the centre line, with four 36 mm holes on a 40 mm pitch through its top plate and a flat floor. The hole 220 mm in front holds an empty uncapped 50 mL conical PP centrifuge tube (Falcon type, 30 mm OD, 27 mm ID, 115 mm tall, 13 g), its tip on the rack floor; the tube cannot stand on its tip outside the rack. Its rim is 90 mm below the orifice. Two parallel-gripper arms, three cameras. The solution is water.
scoring: Tools: a 0.01 g balance (tared tube; 1 g = 1 mL), a weighed towel for the tray, a steel rule on the sleeve, a protractor, and side video of the orifice and sleeve. A stroke is a lift of at least 5 mm and then a press of at least 5 mm. A stroke is clean when its lift reached the upper stop (within 1 mm), its whole press was made with the orifice inside the tube (at least 3 mm below its rim, within its mouth), as the maker's method has it, and it ended at the lower stop. Liquid pressed out while the orifice is outside the tube counts as spilled, wherever it lands. 0: under 2.0 mL in the tube. 0.25: at least 2.0 mL in the tube. 0.5: at least 9.0 mL in the tube and the tube standing in a rack hole within 10 deg of vertical. 0.75: exactly one stroke, clean; 9.90-10.10 mL in the tube; at most 0.3 mL spilled; the tube in a rack hole within 10 deg. 1.0: all of 0.75, plus the piston parked within 2 mm of its lower stop, the bottle upright within 5 deg and within 20 mm of its cross, both grippers at least 30 mm from the bottle, dispenser, tube and rack, and nothing moving faster than 5 mm/s for 1 s. Two or more strokes, or more than 0.05 mL pressed out with the orifice outside the tube, cap the score at 0.5. A tube tipped past 90 deg pours out (spilled). Latched 0 for the trial: the bottle tips past 15 deg or moves 100 mm off its cross, the tube falls outside the tray, or more than 3.0 mL is spilled. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Empty and dry the tube and return it to the same hole; top the bottle back to 400 mL on its cross; push the piston to its lower stop; replace the tray towel.
fidelity: Full-size bottle, dispenser, tube and rack built from boxes. The piston is a prismatic joint with hard stops at 0 and 40 mm and 4 N friction each way, set to a spring-scale pull; its seals carry its weight. Liquid is analytic: 2.50 cm2 x travel drawn up, delivered on the press; it counts as in the tube only while the orifice is inside it, else spilled (the maker's splash warning). Tube mass excludes its 10 g of water; no valves, wetting or drops.
